statement: The Chinese HBM shortage is attributed to U.S. export controls implemented in December 2024, pushing buyers into grey-market channels at several times international prices.
why: Export controls are what split the market in two: they cut a roughly $50 billion domestic chip sector off from normal memory supply and equally foreclose that market to controlled Western parts.

impact.mechanism: Controls foreclose China revenue for controlled accelerators and memory while also throttling the domestic substitute, so the demand that would otherwise flow to merchant GPUs stays out of reach.

evidence.excerpt: the shortage stems from U.S. export controls implemented in December 2024 restricting advanced HBM exports to China

confidence.basis: Single secondary wire exclusive; policy background is summarised rather than sourced to the rule text.
